Add keys to both locales in src/i18n.ts: `setValueTo: 'Değeri {{value}} yap'` (tr) / `'Set value to {{value}}'` (en). Line 251 -> `aria-label={t('setValueTo', { value: stepValue })}`. Line 185 -> replace `'value'` fallback with a localized generic key (add `value: 'Değer' / 'Value'`) or `t('intensity')`.
notes: VERIFIED real by reading the whole component. No useTranslation present. Line 251 'Set value to ' and line 185 || 'value' both confirmed verbatim. setValueTo key does not exist in i18n.ts (grep returned nothing). Medium severity is fair: a11y-only impact (no visible-text regression), affects screen-reader users in Turkish. Note the deferred-items list mentions slider ARIA was partially addressed by the prior pass — this is a genuine remaining gap.

title: t() calls carry hardcoded Turkish defaultValue strings — maintenance/parity risk
problem: Confirmed pattern: many `t('key', { defaultValue: 'Turkish text' })` calls with Turkish-only defaults. Verified samples are Turkish: ConflictResolutionDialog.tsx:62 'Yerel versiyon korundu', :210 'Yerel Versiyonu Koru'; MigrationPrompt.tsx:47 'Anılarınızı Aktaralım mı?', :52 interpolates `${count}` into a Turkish template, :81 'Bu ${count} anı sonsuza kadar silinecek...'. I confirmed the keys DO exist in both tr+en (e.g. conflictResolvedLocal at i18n.ts:1102/2201, keepLocal 1107/2206, migrationPromptTitle 1126/2225), so there is no broken render today. The risk is structural/latent: if a key is renamed/removed, English users silently get the Turkish defaultValue with no missing-key signal.
fix: Treat i18n.ts as single source of truth: remove the inline Turkish defaultValue args (keys already exist), or at minimum replace Turkish defaults with English/neutral ones so a missing key never surfaces Turkish to English users. Add a CI/test check that every `t('key')` reference is defined in both locales. Low priority — no current user-visible defect.
notes: VERIFIED real but the headline count is inflated: the finding says '113 calls across the listed files' — actual grep of defaultValue: across src/components is 69 occurrences total, spread over 9 files (including SettingsSheet, VaultFilters, VaultHeader not all in the finding's list). The substance (Turkish defaults, keys currently exist, latent parity risk) is accurate. Correctly rated low severity since it is a maintenance/latent risk with no live defect. Effort raised to medium because removing/auditing dozens of defaultValue args plus adding a CI check is more than trivial. Not a blocker.

title: Recharts axis tick labels unreadable in dark mode (low contrast)
problem: Confirmed at the code level. All four XAxis/YAxis (lines 337-338 for Monthly Trend BarChart, 398-399 for Intensity BarChart) set only className="text-xs sm:text-sm". Tailwind text-* utilities emit CSS `color`, which recharts axis ticks ignore — tick <text> color comes from the SVG `fill` attribute. With no `tick={{fill}}` override, recharts uses its default tick fill (#666). On the dark card background (dark:bg-gray-800 = #1f2937) #666 yields ~2.8:1 contrast, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 text minimum, so axis labels (months, intensity buckets, count scale) are hard to read in dark mode.
fix: Pass an explicit theme-aware fill to each axis instead of relying on className. Either render a custom tick with className="fill-gray-500 dark:fill-gray-400" (fill-* utilities DO target SVG fill), or read the dark theme and set tick={{ fill: isDark ? '#9CA3AF' : '#4B5563', fontSize: 12 }} plus a matching stroke on the axis line. Apply to all four axes.
notes: Verified Statistics.tsx lines 334-342 (Monthly) and 395-403 (Intensity): both XAxis/YAxis carry only text-* className, no tick prop. Card bg is dark:bg-gray-800 (line 328/389). Real WCAG dark-mode failure; prior audit did not touch these. Severity high justified — affects every axis label on two charts.

title: Page content clipped behind bottom nav on notched devices (pb-16 omits safe-area inset)
problem: Confirmed. The fixed bottom <nav> (Layout.tsx:58-65) has an inner flex row of h-16 (64px, line 66) PLUS style paddingBottom: var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px) (line 63), so its real occupied height is 64px + inset. The scroll container <main> (line 50) reserves clearance with the static class pb-16 (64px) only — no safe-area inset. So on notched / gesture-nav devices the bottom inset band (typically 20-34px) of page content sits under the nav's safe-area padding and cannot be scrolled into view. index.css confirms --safe-area-inset-bottom = env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (line 10), used with calc elsewhere (lines 315/324).
fix: Make main's bottom padding include the inset when the nav is shown: replace the 'pb-16' branch with style={{ paddingBottom: 'calc(4rem + var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))' }} (keep '' for isFullscreenChat), or add a .pb-nav utility doing the calc and apply it.
notes: Verified Layout.tsx:50 main uses static pb-16; nav has inline safe-area paddingBottom at line 63 and h-16 inner row at line 66. Real, but downgraded high->medium: only the inset band (~20-34px on affected devices, 0px on most phones/web) is clipped, not the full nav — the 64px pb-16 clears the nav body. Impact device-conditional and small in magnitude.

title: Destructive photo-delete button tap target ~26px (under 44px) on mobile
problem: Confirmed. The per-photo delete button (MemoryFormPhotos.tsx:225-236) is className="...rounded-full p-1.5...touch-manipulation" wrapping <X size={14}> (line 235): 14px icon + 2x6px padding ≈ 26px hit area, well below the 44px minimum the project's own .touch-target utility enforces (index.css:268-271). It is opacity-100 on mobile (sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100), so on touch devices this is the always-visible primary control to remove a just-added photo. Has touch-manipulation but not touch-target.
fix: Add the existing .touch-target class (min 44x44) plus inline-flex items-center justify-center, or bump padding to ~p-2.5 with a larger icon. Class already defined index.css:268 and used elsewhere.
notes: Verified MemoryFormPhotos.tsx:233 className contains 'rounded-full p-1.5 opacity-100 ... touch-manipulation' with X size={14} at line 235. touch-target confirmed index.css:268. Real. Medium given destructive nature + sub-26px target.

title: Modal/form close (X) buttons under 44px tap target
problem: Confirmed in substance, with one corrected line reference. (a) ConfirmationDialog.tsx:104-110: dismiss X is 'p-1 touch-manipulation' + X size={20} ≈ 28px — no touch-target. (b) DateRangePicker.tsx:192-201: clear button 'p-1 ... rounded-full' + X size={16} ≈ 24px — no touch-target. (c) The cited MemoryForm.tsx:1306 is actually the UNSAVED-CHANGES dialog dismiss (p-1 + size20 ≈28px, also sub-44, real). The true MemoryForm HEADER close X is at lines 766-772: w-8 h-8 (32px), also under 44px and missing touch-target. All are frequently-tapped cancel/close/clear controls.
fix: Add 'touch-target' (index.css:268, min 44x44) and inline-flex items-center justify-center to: ConfirmationDialog X (line 106), DateRangePicker clear (line 197), MemoryForm header close (line 766/768), and the MemoryForm dirty-confirm X (line 1306). Or increase padding to ~p-2.5.
notes: Verified: ConfirmationDialog.tsx:106 'p-1 touch-manipulation'; DateRangePicker.tsx:197 'p-1 ... rounded-full'; MemoryForm.tsx:766-768 header close is 'w-8 h-8' (32px) — this is the real header X, audit's line 1306 is the dirty-confirm dialog X (also sub-44). Corrected header ref to line 766. All genuinely below 44px. Real, medium.

title: Infinite framer-motion animation on Statistics empty state ignores prefers-reduced-motion
problem: Confirmed. Statistics.tsx:209-215 empty-state icon runs animate={{ scale: [1,1.1,1] }} with transition repeat: Infinity and no prefersReducedMotion guard. Framer Motion drives this via JS-set inline transforms, not a CSS animation, so the global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) duration-clamp in index.css does not stop it. Grep for prefersReducedMotion/usePrefersReducedMotion in Statistics.tsx returned NO matches, confirming the page has no reduced-motion handling, while Home (FAB pulse) and Aiya (avatar) do — an inconsistency that breaks the reduced-motion contract.
fix: Read the existing prefersReducedMotion hook value and gate the loop: animate={prefersReducedMotion ? undefined : { scale: [1,1.1,1] }} and conditionally drop the repeat:Infinity transition, matching the Home/Aiya pattern.
notes: Verified Statistics.tsx:209-215 scale loop with repeat:Infinity; grep confirms no prefersReducedMotion usage in the file. Real but downgraded medium->low: single decorative icon on an empty state shown only when there are zero memories — low exposure, purely cosmetic. Valid a11y/consistency gap.

title: Aiya scroll-to-bottom FAB uses hardcoded bottom:100px without safe-area inset
problem: Confirmed. Aiya.tsx:1348-1357 scroll-down FAB is positioned style={{ bottom: '100px' }} (line 1354, hardcoded). The input bar directly below (lines 1362-1364) uses paddingBottom: isKeyboardOpen ? '0px' : 'var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)', so on notched / gesture-nav devices the input bar grows taller by the inset while the FAB stays pinned at 100px, shrinking the gap or overlapping the input/suggestion-chip area. Unlike Home's FAB it does not track the inset. The FAB already carries touch-target (line 1353), so this is purely positioning.
fix: Compute the offset with the inset: style={{ bottom: 'calc(100px + var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))' }}, so the FAB tracks the input-bar height across devices.
notes: Verified Aiya.tsx:1354 bottom:'100px' literal; input bar inset paddingBottom at line 1364. Real but low: only affects devices with a nonzero bottom inset, worst case a reduced gap not a hard clip or unusable control. Cosmetic spacing inconsistency.

title: getUniqueConnections recomputed on every keystroke (flatMap+dedupe over all memories)
problem: VaultFilters.tsx:59 calls `const uniqueConnections = getUniqueConnections(memories)` unconditionally in the render body with no useMemo. memoryUtils.ts:7-9 does `dedupeConnections(memories.flatMap(m => m.connections))` — an O(n) flatMap allocation + normalization pass. VaultFilters receives `searchQuery` as a prop (Vault.tsx:211) wired to setSearchQuery, a synchronous useState update fired on every keystroke (the 300ms debounce in useMemoryFilters only gates the filter recompute, NOT the controlled input re-render). So every character typed re-renders VaultFilters and re-runs the full flatMap+dedupe over the entire unpaginated memory array on the keypress path.
fix: Wrap in useMemo: `const uniqueConnections = useMemo(() => getUniqueConnections(memories), [memories])` and add `useMemo` to the existing `import { useState } from 'react'`. memories only changes on load/save, so dedupe runs once per data change instead of per keystroke.
notes: VERIFIED. Line 59 confirmed verbatim, no useMemo. memoryUtils.ts:7-9 confirmed flatMap+dedupe. Vault.tsx:25 useMemories holds full array; :211 passes searchQuery prop; useMemoryFilters.ts:58 debounce is on debouncedSearchQuery only — raw searchQuery state (and thus VaultFilters re-render) is NOT debounced, so the claim holds. Severity lowered high->medium: the rendered connections list only shows when the filters panel is expanded (isExpanded default false, line 127), but the computation at line 59 runs on every render regardless, so the wasted work is real on the keystroke path even when collapsed. Real but bounded by typical connection counts.

title: Home recomputes core-memory count inline (twice) on every render
problem: Home.tsx:687 (`key={memories.filter(m => m.isCore).length}`) and :692 (`{memories.filter(m => m.isCore).length}`) both run a full O(n) filter over the entire loaded memory array, twice per render, in the render body. Home owns several frequently-changing state values (isBreathing, randomMemory, streak, dailyQuestion, showForm, FAB position) so it re-renders often, and Home loads the full memory list, so each render does two redundant scans.
fix: `const coreCount = useMemo(() => memories.filter(m => m.isCore).length, [memories])` and use coreCount for both the motion.p key and the displayed value.
notes: VERIFIED. Lines 687 and 692 confirmed verbatim — two identical inline filters. Severity lowered medium->low: a single .filter over a typical memory array is cheap; doing it twice is wasteful but not user-perceptible unless the library is very large. Trivial fix, low impact — a cleanup item, not a real perf hotspot.

title: Vault loads the entire memory table into memory on every mount — no Dexie pagination; no list virtualization
problem: memoryService.getAll (memoryService.ts:139-142) does `db.memories.where('userId').equals(userId).toArray()` — pulls the COMPLETE memory set (text, connections, inline base64/local photo arrays) into a JS array. useMemories.ts:46-47 stores the whole array. useMemoryFilters.ts:61 copies it (`[...memories]`) and runs up to six filter passes plus a sort on every filter change. Vault.tsx:35 displayCount defaults to 20 and VaultMemoryList.tsx:97 slices `memories.slice(0, displayCount)` — pure UI windowing that does NOT reduce the Dexie read or heap. handleLoadMore (Vault.tsx:184-190) only bumps displayCount. No virtualization: VaultMemoryList maps the sliced window inside AnimatePresence so DOM grows unbounded as the user loads more. This is the explicitly-deferred 'Vault getPage pagination' item, still unaddressed.
fix: Add `getPage({userId, offset, limit})` to memoryService using a compound Dexie index (e.g. [userId+date]) with `.offset().limit()`, and drive Vault's paging from Dexie instead of fetching everything. For the rendered window add virtualization (react-window/virtua). At minimum push category/lifeArea/date filtering into the Dexie query so the in-memory filter chain doesn't scan the full table. Caveat: text-search and connection filters can't be expressed as Dexie indexes, so a pragmatic first step is virtualizing the rendered list + indexed filtering for index-friendly filters.
notes: VERIFIED all four call sites. getAll:139-142 confirmed toArray() with no limit. useMemories.ts:46 confirmed. Vault.tsx:35 displayCount=20, :188 load-more bumps count, :241 passes filteredMemories (full filtered set). VaultMemoryList.tsx:97 slice inside AnimatePresence confirmed — no virtualization. useMemoryFilters.ts:61 `[...memories]` copy confirmed. Genuine architectural gap matching the deferred-items list. High severity justified for heavy journalers; moderate for typical users. Largest real perf item in this batch.

title: Statistics monthly bucketing parses date-only strings as UTC, diverging from parseLocalDate used everywhere else
problem: Statistics.tsx:145 does `const memoryDate = new Date(m.date)` where m.date is a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' string. Per ES spec `new Date('2026-06-01')` parses as UTC midnight, so in timezones behind UTC it resolves to the previous local day, mis-bucketing memories near a month boundary into the adjacent month. It is compared against monthStart/monthEnd built with local-time `new Date(year, month, ...)` (lines 141-142), a mixed-zone comparison. The rest of the app uses parseLocalDate (useMemoryFilters.ts:76-83) to avoid this; parseLocalDate exists at dateFormat.ts:21.
fix: Import parseLocalDate from '../utils/dateFormat' and use `const memoryDate = parseLocalDate(m.date)` at Statistics.tsx:145, consistent with useMemoryFilters.
notes: VERIFIED. Statistics.tsx:145 confirmed `new Date(m.date)`. monthStart/monthEnd at 141-142 use local-time constructors, so UTC-parsed date vs local-time bounds is the mixed-zone bug. parseLocalDate confirmed at dateFormat.ts:21. This is a correctness bug (wrong analytics), not strictly perf, but real. Timezone-conditional: only affects boundary-dated entries in UTC-or-behind zones (positive-UTC zones map to the same local calendar day, no shift). Medium is appropriate.

title: compressImage default 1920px/0.8 keeps inline base64 photos heavy through getAll/filters/sync
problem: compressImage (imageUtils.ts:50) defaults to maxWidth 1920 / quality 0.8, and MemoryForm.tsx:617 calls it explicitly with (file, 1920, 0.8). A 1920px AVIF/WebP data-URL is still sizeable; that base64 string is carried in the in-memory Memory array (getAll, the [...memories] filter copies, sort) and JSON-stringified into syncQueueV2 payloads until a successful sync. This compounds perf-3 for offline/pre-sync state.
fix: Lower the gallery default to ~1280px / ~0.7 (pass from MemoryForm.tsx:617, or change imageUtils defaults). Note the Storage migration the finding requested is ALREADY implemented (uploadLocalPhotos on sync), so only the encode dimensions remain as a lever.
notes: VERIFIED with correction. The finding's premise that photos are NEVER migrated off base64 is OUTDATED — memoryService.ts:310-315 (uploadLocalPhotos + ref swap on sync) already moves them to Storage and persists URLs back (prior-pass work). So in-memory weight is transient (until sync), not permanent. avifSupport memoization claim is correct (imageUtils.ts:3,21-44). Remaining real lever is just the 1920/0.8 dimensions; impact low because compression already happens and Storage migration exists. Borderline isReal; marked true since the oversized default is a genuine (if minor) pre-sync heap/payload cost. The dimension tweak is low-risk, not a defect.

title: Aiya usage refund is a non-atomic absolute write that can grant free messages under concurrency
problem: meterUsage() (index.ts:300-323) reserves a slot via the atomic RPC increment_aiya_usage, which does SET aiya_messages_used = aiya_messages_used + 1 (migration 20260620050000, lines 29-33). But refundUsage() (index.ts:326-335) writes the ABSOLUTE snapshot value: update({ aiya_messages_used: Math.max(0, usageUsed) }) where usageUsed was captured at request start (index.ts:255). It is called from the catch block at index.ts:617 only when an action was metered. Since chat/analysis share the burst bucket allowing 20 req/60s (RATE_CHAT_MAX), concurrent requests are expected. If request A's OpenAI call fails after reserving, A's refund overwrites the counter back to A's stale snapshot, silently wiping any increment request B applied in between. The user gets a free metered message. This re-introduces the exact read-then-write race the migration was written to eliminate.
fix: Add a SECURITY DEFINER RPC decrement_aiya_usage(p_user uuid) doing UPDATE public.users SET aiya_messages_used = GREATEST(0, aiya_messages_used - 1) WHERE id = p_user, with the same REVOKE-from-public/anon/authenticated + GRANT EXECUTE TO service_role grants as increment_aiya_usage, and call it from refundUsage() via supabaseAdmin.rpc('decrement_aiya_usage', { p_user: userId }) instead of the absolute update. Never write an absolute snapshot back to a concurrently-mutated counter.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed increment RPC is atomic (migration lines 29-33). Confirmed refundUsage at index.ts:328-331 writes Math.max(0, usageUsed) where usageUsed = userRow.aiya_messages_used snapshot from index.ts:255. Confirmed no decrement_aiya_usage RPC exists in any migration. Confirmed refund is gated on metered flag (only chat/analysis) and the burst limiter permits concurrency (RATE_CHAT_MAX=20/60s). Highest-value finding; sits squarely in the billing path the prior pass hardened. Severity high is justified — direct revenue/quota correctness hole, though it requires the relatively narrow window of a failing OpenAI call concurrent with a succeeding one.

title: Two divergent platform-detection helpers (isNative vs isNativePlatform) that can return opposite answers
problem: isNativePlatform() (platform.ts:7-21) returns true if window.Capacitor exists OR, as a fallback, if window.CapacitorPlugins exists (lines 16-18). isNative() (capacitor.ts:170-179) only checks window.Capacitor and omits the CapacitorPlugins fallback. notificationService imports isNativePlatform (confirmed import at line 3, used at lines 25/48/78/124/226/336/434/507), while memorySyncService (line 1) and haptic (line 6) import isNative. In a boot state where the plugins proxy is injected before the Capacitor global, the two helpers disagree, producing split-brain platform branching within one session. Duplicated logic that drifts violates CLAUDE.md 2.6 intent.
fix: Make capacitor.ts a thin re-export: export { isNativePlatform as isNative } from './platform' (or align isNative's body to include the CapacitorPlugins fallback), so there is a single source of truth and all callers behave identically.
notes: VERIFIED REAL as a duplication/drift issue. Both helpers and all three import sites confirmed exactly as described. Downgraded severity from medium to low: the divergence only manifests in the narrow window where window.CapacitorPlugins is present while window.Capacitor is absent — in standard Capacitor builds both globals are injected together by the runtime, so in practice the two agree. The real defect is maintainability/duplication, not an observed production bug. Fix is trivial and worth doing.

title: Web daily-reminder scheduling leaks setTimeout timers and fires duplicate notifications
problem: scheduleDailyReminder's web path (notificationService.ts:318-331), its scheduleNext closure (304-315), and the native-fallback path (232-240) each create a setTimeout and store the id in localStorage reminder_timeout_${userId} WITHOUT first clearing the previously stored timer. Contrast scheduleRandomMemoryReminder (411-414) which clears the existing interval before creating a new one — daily reminder has no such guard. Home.tsx's setupNotifications (133-139) depends on streak.currentStreak, and the effect at Home.tsx:184-188 re-runs whenever setupNotifications changes, so every streak change re-schedules a new live timer while only the latest id is tracked. cancelReminder (461-465) can only clear the last stored id. Result on web/PWA: orphaned timers fire stale duplicate daily-reminder notifications and accumulate over a session. Native repeating-notification path is unaffected (it calls cancelReminder at line 245 before scheduling).
fix: At the top of the web scheduling path in scheduleDailyReminder, read reminder_timeout_${userId} and clearTimeout it before creating the new timeout (mirroring scheduleRandomMemoryReminder lines 411-414). Apply the same to the native-fallback branch at line 240. Optionally guard/debounce setupNotifications so it does not re-fire on every streak.currentStreak change.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed: web path (318-331) and scheduleNext (304-315) overwrite localStorage without clearing; native-fallback (232-240) same. scheduleRandomMemoryReminder DOES clear first (411-414), confirming the inconsistency. Home.tsx setupNotifications deps include streak.currentStreak (line 139) and the effect re-runs on it (line 188). cancelReminder only clears the single stored id. Medium severity appropriate: web/PWA-only, but causes real duplicate notifications and timer accumulation, a user-visible defect.

title: setHasCompletedOnboarding does unguarded localStorage.setItem, inconsistent with every other store setter
problem: setTheme (useStore.ts:85-98) and setLanguage (100-121) wrap localStorage.setItem in try/catch with a DEV warn (the documented 'localStorage might be disabled, fail silently' pattern). setHasCompletedOnboarding (123-126) calls localStorage.setItem('hasCompletedOnboarding', completed.toString()) with NO try/catch. On a WebView/device where localStorage is disabled or quota-exceeded, this throws synchronously inside the Zustand setter, breaking the onboarding-completion action while sibling setters degrade gracefully.
fix: Wrap the setItem in setHasCompletedOnboarding in the same try/catch + DEV-warn block used by setTheme/setLanguage, then call set({ hasCompletedOnboarding: completed }) regardless so state updates even if persistence fails.
notes: VERIFIED REAL exactly as described — line numbers match. Low severity is correct: localStorage being unavailable is an edge case (private mode / quota), but the inconsistency with sibling setters is undeniable and the fix is a 4-line wrap.

title: useNotifications subscribes to i18n via unused useTranslation()/t
problem: useNotifications imports useTranslation (line 2) and destructures const { t } = useTranslation() (line 18) but never calls t anywhere in the hook (confirmed: no t( usage in the file). The hook only forwards already-localized message strings to toast. Besides being dead code, useTranslation subscribes every consumer component to i18n language-change events, forcing needless re-renders of all toast-using components on language switch.
fix: Remove the import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next' line and the const { t } = useTranslation() line (18). The hook needs no i18n subscription.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Read entire file (92 lines): t is declared at line 18 and never referenced; all show* helpers take a pre-localized message: string argument. Dead code plus an unnecessary i18n re-render subscription. Low severity accurate. Side note: this surviving means TS noUnusedLocals is likely not enforcing here, otherwise the build would flag t — worth being aware of but out of scope for this finding.

title: Default Aiya message limit (50) and default language/theme duplicated across client and edge with no shared constant
problem: New-user defaults are hardcoded in two independent places. The edge function defines DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50 (index.ts:22) and uses it plus language:'tr', theme:'light' when upserting a missing user (index.ts:241,244,245). userService.ensureUserExists hardcodes the same literals independently: aiya_messages_limit: 50 (userService.ts:122), language: 'tr' (125), theme: 'light' (126). If the free-tier quota or default locale changes, the two paths drift and users get mismatched defaults depending on which path created the row. Config values per CLAUDE.md 1.14/2.10.
fix: On the client, define a shared constants module (e.g. src/lib/userDefaults.ts exporting DEFAULT_AIYA_LIMIT = 50, DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = 'tr', DEFAULT_THEME = 'light') and reference it in userService. On the edge, reuse the existing DEFAULT_LIMIT constant for the upsert (currently the upsert at line 241 already uses DEFAULT_LIMIT, but language/theme are inline literals — promote them to constants too). Document the canonical values so both sides stay aligned.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed userService.ts:122/125/126 literals and index.ts:22 DEFAULT_LIMIT + 241/244/245 usage. Note: the edge function already routes the limit through the DEFAULT_LIMIT constant (only language/theme are inline literals there), so the worst duplication is between client literals and edge constant. Low severity correct — both default rows are currently identical so there's no live bug; this is a forward-looking maintainability/config-hygiene issue. confidence rightly medium in original.

title: Android back button cannot exit the app from home — exitApp never wired
problem: Confirmed. Layout.handleBackButton returns false on '/' to 'let native handle (exit app)' (Layout.tsx:24-27). But the native backButton listener (capacitor.ts:379-391) only does `if (window.history.length > 1) window.history.back()` and explicitly comments 'exitApp is not available in our AppPlugin interface'. The AppPlugin interface in src/types/capacitor.ts:27 has getLaunchUrl but NO exitApp. So at the root with history.length===1, back does nothing (no nav, no exit). With singleTask launchMode and a typical SPA history depth >1, back() will instead walk SPA history, which is mildly confusing rather than the expected leave-app behavior.
fix: Add `exitApp(): Promise<void>` to AppPlugin in src/types/capacitor.ts, expose it in loadApp() (both window-plugin and dynamic-import branches in capacitor.ts), and restructure the backButton listener: if backButtonHandler() returns true -> handled; else if window.history.length>1 -> history.back(); else await App.exitApp(). @capacitor/app is already a dependency so no new package is needed.
notes: VERIFIED: AppPlugin interface (src/types/capacitor.ts) confirmed to expose only getLaunchUrl, not exitApp. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is a polish/UX deviation from Android norms, not a crash or data issue, and in practice history.length is usually >1 so back navigates rather than dead-stops. Still a genuine, easily-fixable native UX gap.

title: scheduleRandomMemoryReminder is uncancellable AND dead code
problem: Confirmed on both counts. scheduleRandomMemoryReminder (line 334) schedules 4 repeating daily native notifications with ids notificationId(userId,2)+0..3 (lines 386-396, every:'day', repeats:true). No method cancels these: cancelReminder (432) only cancels id prefix 1; cancelStreakProtection (572) only cancels id prefix 3. There is no cancelRandomMemory. A project-wide grep shows scheduleRandomMemoryReminder has ZERO callers — it is only defined, never invoked. The web branch also stores a setInterval id in localStorage whose in-memory handle is lost on reload, so the stored id cannot clear the live interval.
fix: Since it is unused, the cleanest fix is to delete scheduleRandomMemoryReminder entirely to remove the latent uncancellable-notification bug. If the feature is wanted later, add a cancelRandomMemory(userId) that cancels ids notificationId(userId,2)+0..3 natively and clears+removes the stored web interval, and wire scheduling/cancellation into the settings notification toggle.
notes: VERIFIED dead code: grep for scheduleRandomMemoryReminder returns only the definition at notificationService.ts:334. Real latent bug but severity is low because the code path is never reached in the shipped app — it's dormant. The auditor's 'ships an uncancellable notification' worst case requires someone wiring it up first.

title: Streak-protection native notification is never cancelled when user changes/clears reminders
problem: Confirmed. Home.tsx:91-97 calls scheduleStreakProtection on every load when currentStreak>0 (one-shot 20:00 notification, id prefix 3). SettingsSheet.handleSaveReminders (line 139-148) only calls cancelReminder(user.id) — it never calls cancelStreakProtection. Grep confirms cancelStreakProtection's only callers are internal (notificationService.ts:525 self-call before re-scheduling) — no UI path invokes it. So a user has no way to stop the streak-protection ping from settings. NOTE the practical blast radius is small: scheduleStreakProtection only fires when daysSinceLastMemory===1 (notificationService.ts:486), it cancels+reschedules itself on each Home load (line 525), and it self-resolves once the user adds a memory (daysSinceLastMemory===0 early-returns).
fix: Add notificationService.cancelStreakProtection(user.id) to SettingsSheet's reminder-disable path, and add an explicit notifications on/off control that cancels BOTH reminder types. Optionally skip scheduleStreakProtection in Home.tsx when the user's daily_reminder_time is unset.
notes: VERIFIED: SettingsSheet handleSaveReminders read (lines 139-182) — only cancelReminder is called, confirmed no cancelStreakProtection. Home.tsx:91-97 confirmed unconditional scheduling on currentStreak>0. Severity lowered medium->low: it is a single self-limiting once-a-day notification (it does not repeat — schedule has no `repeats` flag, only `at`, line 533-535), so it is not a persistent uncancellable nag like CAP-03 would be.

title: USE_EXACT_ALARM is a Play-policy risk; no canScheduleExactAlarms handling
problem: Partially confirmed with one important correction. Manifest declares both SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM (line 54) and USE_EXACT_ALARM (line 55). The USE_EXACT_ALARM concern is REAL and the strongest part of this finding: on Android 14+ USE_EXACT_ALARM is reserved for alarm/clock-category apps and Google Play flags/rejects other categories — a journaling app should not declare it. CORRECTION to the auditor's framing: the daily reminder (notificationService.ts:250-266) uses schedule.repeats=true/every='day', which Capacitor LocalNotifications implements as an INEXACT repeating alarm, NOT an exact alarm — so the 'daily reminder silently never fires' claim is overstated for the repeating reminder. The streak-protection notification (lines 527-542) is the one-shot `at` schedule that would use an exact alarm path. There is indeed no canScheduleExactAlarms() check and SecurityException is only caught/logged generically (lines 543-549).
fix: Remove USE_EXACT_ALARM from AndroidManifest.xml (primary fix — eliminates the Play review risk; this app is not a clock/alarm app). The daily reminder is fine on inexact scheduling. For streak protection, either accept inexact timing (a 20:00 nudge does not need second-precision) and drop SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM too, or keep SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM and add a canScheduleExactAlarms() check that routes the user to system settings with a localized (i18n) explanation when denied, instead of swallowing the failure as a warning log.
notes: VERIFIED manifest lines 54-55 both present. Kept at medium: the Play Store policy risk on USE_EXACT_ALARM is legitimate and can block release. Downgraded the auditor's reliability claim — the repeating daily reminder is inexact by Capacitor design so it will fire; the exact-alarm denial path mainly affects the self-limiting streak-protection one-shot.

title: Notification permission denial swallowed — success toast shown even when denied
problem: Confirmed. handleSaveReminders (SettingsSheet.tsx:146) calls `await notificationService.requestPermission()` and discards the returned boolean, then unconditionally schedules (line 147) and later shows toast.success(t('settingsSaved')) (lines 155/174). requestPermission() returns false on denial (notificationService.ts:84/94/119). So a user who denies POST_NOTIFICATIONS is told their reminder was saved successfully when no notification will ever be delivered. NOTE: there is a separate handleEnableNotifications path (SettingsSheet.tsx:184-189) that DOES handle the boolean correctly with notificationPermissionDenied/notificationsEnabled toasts — so the i18n keys already exist; only the save-reminders path ignores the result.
fix: In handleSaveReminders, capture `const granted = await notificationService.requestPermission()`; if !granted, show toast.error(t('notificationPermissionDenied')) (key already exists) and skip claiming success / optionally still persist the time but warn. Only show settingsSaved when granted.
notes: VERIFIED: SettingsSheet.tsx lines 139-182 (save path ignores boolean) vs lines 184-189 (enable path uses it correctly), confirming both the bug and that the needed i18n keys already exist. Low severity: misleading-success UX, not data loss; trivial to fix.

title: OAuth browser-fallback cold-start can hang the spinner — getLaunchUrl not consulted
problem: Confirmed as a narrow edge case. The browser-fallback path (useOAuth.ts:288-328) registers an appUrlOpen listener (line 100) but never calls App.getLaunchUrl() on mount (the useEffect at line 89-191 only sets up the live listener). If the OAuth redirect cold-starts a killed activity, the callback URL arrives as the launch URL before React mounts and is lost; exchangeCodeForSession never runs and loadingRef/setLoading stay true with no timeout to reset. As the auditor correctly notes, the PRIMARY native flow uses the Credential Manager (SocialLogin, lines 209-276) which never opens a browser, so this only affects the browser fallback — and that fallback only triggers if native init fails or on web (where cold-start launch-URL semantics don't apply). getLaunchUrl IS already available (defined in AppPlugin interface src/types/capacitor.ts:30 and exposed in capacitor.ts loadApp).
fix: In the native useEffect, after setting up the appUrlOpen listener, also call App.getLaunchUrl(); if its url matches the com.nicebase.app://oauth/callback scheme, run the same code/token exchange logic. Add a safety timeout in handleOAuthLogin's browser branch that resets loading and shows t('oauthError') if no callback arrives within ~60s.
notes: VERIFIED: getLaunchUrl present in AppPlugin interface (src/types/capacitor.ts:30) and in loadApp (capacitor.ts:84,95) but grep/read of useOAuth.ts shows it is never called — only the appUrlOpen listener. Real but low severity: the primary login path (native Credential Manager) is unaffected; this bites only the rarely-exercised browser fallback on a killed-app cold start. A reset timeout is the higher-value half of the fix.
